draft.title: Christianity in medieval Europe
card: In medieval western Europe, most people were Catholic Christians. The Catholic Church was led by the Pope, who was based in Rome.
The Church shaped daily life. Church bells marked the hours, and people went to Mass, were baptised and married in church, and kept holy days.
The Church shaped learning and politics. Monks and priests ran most schools and copied books by hand. Kings sought the Pope's support, and church leaders advised rulers.
The Church was rich. It owned large areas of land and collected a tax from people, called the tithe, which was a share of what they earned or grew.
draft.remember: The Church was a powerful and wealthy force in daily life, learning and politics.

a.q: Which fact best explains why the medieval Church was wealthy?
opts: It owned much land and collected a tax called the tithe
It ran most schools and charged families high fees
It took all of the treasure won by kings in war
It controlled trade and sold goods across Europe
a.why: The card says the Church held large areas of land and collected the tithe, a share of what people earned or grew. Running schools is true, but the card does not say it made the Church rich.
a.clue: Think about what the Church owned and what people paid it.

b.q: In a village in 1200, Tom is baptised, his family keeps holy days, and the village priest teaches a few boys to read. What does this show about the Church?
opts: It shaped daily life and learning in the community
It ruled the village as a king would
It gave all villagers equal wealth and land
It had no influence outside the village
b.why: Baptism and holy days show the Church shaping daily life, and the priest teaching reading shows it shaping learning. The card does not say the Church ruled villages as a king would. It says the Church had influence in politics, but in a different way.
b.clue: Look for what the priest and the church do in everyday village life.

a.best: It owned much land and collected a tax called the tithe

b.best: It shaped daily life and learning in the community

problems.detail: The right option is the longest and the only one that uses the card's precise term 'tithe'. The clue ('what the Church owned and what people paid it') also points straight at it, so a student could pick it without understanding the idea.
